title: The son's team
summary: The chairman's son, the one you told the truth to or didn't, manages a Sunday side now. He asks you to come and talk to his players about what it takes. His dad wants to come too.

ends.title: What it takes
ends.text: You talked to the chairman's son's Sunday side. His dad stood at the back and clapped longest.

ends.title: The old favour
ends.text: You went to the chairman's son's Sunday side. He told his players you once lied to him, and that you were right to be sorry.

beats.title: His Sunday side

event.title: His Sunday side
event.speaker: chairman
setup: A text from the chairman's son. He's twenty-six, a physio in the week, and he runs a Sunday side called the Fox. "Would you talk to my lads before the cup? Ten minutes. Dad wants to come. Sorry."

say: {if ended(arc-the-chairmans-son:the-truth)}You told him at nineteen he wasn't good enough. He's thanked you every year since.{/if}{if ended(arc-the-chairmans-son:the-favour)}You told his dad he was nearly there. He wasn't.{/if}

replies.label: "I'll come. And I owe you a sorry."
"I can't, mate. Good luck in the cup."

go.text: A pub function room, sixteen lads in tracksuits, the chairman at the back with a half. You talk for twenty minutes.

sorry.text: You say sorry in front of his lads. He laughs and says he'd have done the same. His dad has to go outside.

no.text: He says no problem. They lose in the cup, four-three.

beats.hint: The chairman's son wants you at his Sunday side

event.title: The cup
event.speaker: chairman
setup: A season on. The Fox are in the county Sunday cup final, and there's a photo of you on the wall of their function room.
{if arc.path=='no'}They lost the cup the year you said you couldn't come. Nobody mentions it.{/if}

outcomes.text: They win on penalties. The son lifts the cup and points at his dad in the crowd.
They win on penalties. In the bar he tells his lads the story of the lie, and you buy a round for it.
